name: Vinvin Force Email
author: vinvin27

sections.description:
You copied a live site to a staging server, or you are building a shop on your laptop. Orders, password resets, form notifications and newsletters are about to be sent to real people. Vinvin Force Email redirects every message sent by WordPress to the one address you choose.

  • One setting: an email address, in Settings > General.
  • Every recipient is replaced, “To”, “Cc” and “Bcc” included. The Cc and Bcc headers are removed, because left in place they would still deliver the message to the real recipients.
  • Nothing is lost: the original recipients are added at the start of the subject, for example [customer@example.com] | Your order.
  • Works with anything that uses wp_mail(): WooCommerce, contact forms, SMTP plugins, password resets.
  • A reminder in the dashboard: while the plugin redirects email, a notice tells administrators where it goes, so nobody forgets it on a live site.
  • Safe by default: with no address (or an invalid one), emails are sent normally.

This plugin is meant for testing and development. Do not leave it active on a live site.

I am a French WordPress developer based in Montreal.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the vinvin-force-email folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to Settings > General, fill in “Force email” and save.
sections.faq:
Will my customers receive anything?

No, as long as an address is set. Every message goes to that address only, including copies (Cc) and blind copies (Bcc).

How do I know who the email was meant for?

The original recipients are written at the start of the subject.

How do I turn it off?

Empty the “Force email” field and save, or deactivate the plugin.

Does it work with an SMTP plugin?

Yes. It changes the message before it is handed to the mailer, so any plugin that sends through wp_mail() is covered. A plugin that sends mail by its own means, without wp_mail(), is not.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

Release Date – 28 October 2026

  • Tested with WordPress 7.1 and PHP 8.
  • Fix: Cc and Bcc headers were kept, so the real recipients still received the message. They are now removed and listed in the subject.
  • Fix: a list of recipients caused an “Array to string conversion” warning on PHP 8.
  • Fix: with no address set, all emails were lost. Nothing is changed any more until a valid address is saved.
  • The address is validated and saved as an email address, and escaped when displayed.
  • A dashboard notice shows while emails are redirected.
  • Requires WordPress 5.0 and PHP 7.4.

1.0.0.1

  • Add icon, banner and retina support.

1.0.0.0

  • Initial commit.
  • Basic settings.
